scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: r12 dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3
Mechanism: r12's four /24 loopbacks live on separate Linux
  interfaces (lo, lo1, lo2, lo3) — that's the workaround for
  FRR eigrpd only advertising one prefix per interface. When
  lo1/lo2/lo3 go down, EIGRP withdraws those three prefixes;
  102.1.1.0/24 (on the real `lo`) stays advertised. R11
  withdraws them upstream into OSPF.
Localization: r12
Root cause: dummy interfaces lo1/lo2/lo3 are down on r12
Fix: `ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up`
  on r12
scenario.fix_spec:

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: R12’s local loopback interfaces that source the EIGRP routes. Specifically, loopbacks lo1–lo3 that carry 102.1.2.0/24, 102.1.3.0/24, and 102.1.4.0/24 are down, so EIGRP on R12 no longer originates these prefixes.

Mechanism: R11’s EIGRP adjacency to R12 remains up (R11 shows neighbor 112.1.1.2 on eth0), but R12 is only advertising what it has locally up/up. With lo1–lo3 down, those three /24s are absent from R12’s RIB (R12 ip route shows only 102.1.1.0/24 as connected via lo; 102.1.2/24–102.1.4/24 are missing). R11 redistributes EIGRP into OSPF (router ospf: “redistribute eigrp”), so when those three routes vanished from EIGRP, they were withdrawn from OSPF and disappeared from R1’s RIB. 102.1.1.0/24 persists because it is bound to the primary lo interface on R12, which is up, so it continues to be advertised.

Localization: R12, interfaces lo1, lo2, lo3 (state DOWN per ip addr); R11 OSPF redistribution path to R1 is functioning as designed.

Root cause: The loopback interfaces lo1–lo3 on R12 were administratively brought down (or not brought up), removing their connected routes from EIGRP.

Corrective fix: On R12, bring the loopbacks up (e.g., ip link set lo1 up; ip link set lo2 up; ip link set lo3 up) or move the 102.1.2/24–102.1.4/24 addresses onto an always-up loopback. Verify EIGRP network statements remain present, then confirm R11 learns the prefixes via EIGRP and R1 sees them again via OSPF.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly localizes the problem to R12 (R12’s loopbacks lo1–lo3 are down).
The agent explicitly identifies R12’s loopback dummy interfaces lo1, lo2, and lo3 as the affected components.
Agent explicitly describes the partial-withdrawal pattern: lo1–lo3 prefixes were withdrawn while 102.1.1.0/24 (primary lo) remained advertised.
Recommends bringing lo1–lo3 up on R12 (or moving the addresses to an always-up loopback), which matches the expected fix.
